es: Reconocer las partes de un plan de negocio (resumen, mercado, marketing, operaciones, finanzas, riesgos, equipo) y el lenguaje típico de cada una.

teaching.en: The executive summary opens a business plan in a few lines: what the workshop will do, for whom, and why it should succeed.
teaching.es: El resumen ejecutivo abre un plan de negocio en pocas líneas: qué hará el taller, para quién y por qué debería tener éxito.
teaching.explanationEs: Es la sección más leída; debe poder entenderse sin leer el resto del plan.
segments: The executive summary opens a business plan in a few lines: what
the workshop will do, for whom, and why it should succeed.

teaching.en: The market section names the target market and the competitors already serving it, and explains what makes the newcomer different.
teaching.es: La sección de mercado nombra el mercado objetivo y a los competidores que ya lo atienden, y explica qué hace diferente al recién llegado.
teaching.explanationEs: Fíjate en los grupos de clientes y en las comparaciones con otros negocios.

teaching.en: Marketing explains how the firm will promote itself; operations describe the shifts and suppliers behind the daily work.
teaching.es: El marketing explica cómo se dará a conocer la empresa; las operaciones describen los turnos y proveedores que sostienen el trabajo diario.
teaching.explanationEs: Marketing usa will + verbo base; operations habla de horarios, turnos y rutinas.
segments: Marketing explains how the firm will promote itself; operations
describe the shifts and suppliers behind the daily work.
teaching.audioText: Marketing explains how the firm will promote itself; operations describe the shifts and suppliers behind the daily work.

teaching.en: Finance asks for a loan, tracks cash flow month by month and shows when the business should break even.
teaching.es: Finanzas pide un préstamo, sigue el flujo de caja mes a mes y muestra cuándo debería alcanzar el negocio el punto de equilibrio.
teaching.explanationEs: Break even es alcanzar el punto en que los ingresos igualan a los costes; el beneficio llega después.
segments: Finance asks for a loan, tracks cash flow month by
month and shows when the business should break even.

teaching.en: Every forecast of profit rests on assumptions, so a credible plan states them openly instead of hiding them in a table.
teaching.es: Toda previsión de beneficio se apoya en supuestos, así que un plan creíble los declara abiertamente en lugar de esconderlos en una tabla.
teaching.explanationEs: Los números sin supuestos explícitos suenan más seguros de lo que son.
segments: Every forecast of profit rests on assumptions, so a credible plan
states them openly instead of hiding them in a table.
teaching.audioText: Every forecast of profit rests on assumptions, so a credible plan states them openly instead of hiding them in a table.

teaching.en: The risk section names what may go wrong; the team section shows that a skilled mechanic can deal with it.
teaching.es: La sección de riesgos nombra lo que puede salir mal; la del equipo muestra que un mecánico con experiencia puede afrontarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Riesgos usa may para lo posible pero incierto; el equipo presenta experiencia y funciones.

prompt.es: ¿A qué sección pertenece este fragmento y por qué?

choices.text: Marketing: it explains how customers will hear about the workshop.
Market: it describes who the customers are and who else serves them.
Operations: it sets out the daily routine of the workshop.

feedback.es: Habla de cómo darse a conocer (promote) y de una oferta para atraer clientes: es marketing, no descripción del mercado.

hint.es: Busca el verbo promote: explica cómo darse a conocer.

origin.text: We will promote the workshop through local cycling clubs and a weekly offer for students, and we will measure each campaign by the number of new customers it brings.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nuestro mercado objetivo son estudiantes y trabajadores que van en bici.»

feedback.es: Target market es el grupo de clientes al que se dirige el negocio; aparece en la sección de mercado.

origin.text: Our ___ market is made up of students and workers who cycle every day, and the two competitors in the area ignore them at weekends.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Necesitamos un préstamo para comprar herramientas y pagar el alquiler.»

answer.text: We need a loan to buy tools and pay the rent

feedback.es: La frase pertenece a finanzas: need a loan + to + verbo indica para qué se pide el dinero.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fragmento con la sección del plan a la que pertenece.

pairs: Leo has ten years of experience as a mechanic and has led a team of six.
Each mechanic will work one morning shift and one afternoon shift.
Posters in local cafes and a weekly offer will attract new customers.
Most of our customers are students under thirty who cycle every day.
If costs rise faster than sales, we may have to raise our prices.

feedback.es: Cada fragmento usa el lenguaje de su sección: experiencia, turnos, promoción, clientes y posibles problemas.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué sección procede este fragmento y cómo lo sabes.

choices.text: Marketing: it explains how the firm will make itself known to the public.
Market: it describes the customers and what the competitors do not offer.
Operations: it sets out opening hours and shifts for each worker.

feedback.es: Se habla de clientes y de competidores que no abren los domingos: es la sección de mercado.

origin.audio: Our main customers are commuters who ride to work, and two competitors already repair bicycles in the area. Neither of them opens on Sundays, and that is the chance we intend to take.

prompt.es: Completa: «Esperamos alcanzar el punto de equilibrio en nueve meses.»

feedback.es: Break even significa llegar al punto en que los ingresos cubren los costes; después llega el beneficio.

origin.text: The plan shows cash flow month by month. We expect to ___ even after nine months, and to make a profit from then on.

prompt.es: ¿Qué implica el posible socio sobre este plan?

choices.text: That the executive summary is too vague, so the authors should rewrite it before meeting.
That the risk section is wrong and the market section should be left exactly as it stands.
That two sections seem to disagree with each other and must be made to agree.
That he will not meet the authors until the loan they are asking for has been reduced.

feedback.es: El socio señala que el mercado dice una cosa y los riesgos otra, y pide que las dos secciones concuerden antes de reunirse.

origin.text: A note from a possible partner: The plan is well written, and the executive summary is clear. However, the market section claims that nobody else serves cyclists, while the risk section admits that two competitors already repair bicycles nearby. Either the market has been overstated or the risks have been understated. I would like the authors to make the two sections agree before we meet.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase del plan pertenece a la sección de riesgos.

choices.text: The one about customers who may leave if prices go up.
The one about the loan for tools and rent.
The one about reaching the break-even point after nine months.

feedback.es: Los dos primeros enunciados describen dinero que entra o sale (finanzas); el tercero, sobre clientes que podrían marcharse si suben los precios, es algo que podría salir mal: va en riesgos.

origin.audio: I am checking where each sentence of my business plan belongs, and my partner is helping me. The first says that we need a loan of twelve thousand dollars, which would cover tools and the first three months of rent. The second says that we expect to break even after nine months. My partner points out that those two belong together, because both describe money that comes in or goes out. The last sentence warns that customers might leave if we raise our prices. That one needs a heading of its own, since it is neither a figure nor a promise, but something that could go wrong. I will move each sentence to its right section tonight, and then I will read the whole plan again from the top.

prompt.es: Completa: «El resumen ejecutivo debe sintetizar todo el plan en una sola página.»

feedback.es: Summarise es el verbo preciso para condensar un plan entero en una página.

origin.text: The executive summary should ___ the whole plan on a single page: what the business does, who it serves and why it will work.

prompt.es: Escribe la sección de mercado de una panadería nueva: clientes y competidores.

answer.text: Our target market is office workers who want fresh bread before eight in the morning. Two competitors already sell bread nearby, but neither of them opens before nine, so we will serve customers who are currently ignored.
accepted: Our target market is office workers who want fresh bread before eight in the morning. Two competitors already sell bread nearby, but neither of them opens before nine, so we will serve customers who are currently ignored.
Our target customers are people who work in the offices around the bakery. One competitor already sells bread in the area, but it does not open early, so we will offer fresh bread before work.
Our main customers are office workers who buy bread on their way to work. Two competitors already sell bread in the area, but neither opens before nine, which leaves the early morning open to us.

feedback.es: La sección de mercado describe al cliente objetivo, nombra a los competidores y explica qué espacio queda libre.

origin.text: Tu negocio es una panadería nueva en un barrio de oficinas. Escribe la sección de mercado en dos o tres frases: quiénes son tus clientes objetivo, qué competidores hay y qué no cubren.

prompt.es: ¿A qué sección pertenece esta frase y qué deja entrever?

choices.text: Risks: it names a threat and hints that the workshop depends strongly on its suppliers.
Finance: it reports the workshop's cash flow and the size of the loan it needs.
Market: it compares the workshop's prices with those of its competitors.
Operations: it explains how the workshop buys parts from its suppliers each week.

feedback.es: La frase nombra una amenaza (costes que suben) y revela la dependencia de los proveedores: es la sección de riesgos.

origin.text: If the price of parts rises faster than our sales, the workshop could lose money within a year, and it would have to close unless we find a cheaper supplier.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La sección de finanzas muestra cuándo se llega al equilibrio.»

answer.text: The finance section shows when the business will break even

feedback.es: El sujeto es The finance section y when introduce la pregunta indirecta sobre el momento.

prompt.es: ¿Qué fragmento pertenece a la sección de operaciones?

choices.text: Two competitors already repair bicycles within a kilometre of the station.
The workshop will open six days a week, with two shifts on weekdays.
We will promote the opening with posters and a weekly offer for students.
We need a loan to buy tools and cover the first three months of rent.

feedback.es: Días de apertura y turnos describen el funcionamiento diario: es operaciones; los demás fragmentos son mercado, marketing y finanzas.
